Single-Pass Bacterial & Prophage ORF Prediction

Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655 (GenBank: CP014225.1 — 4,659,625 bp)

Co-predicting bacterial host genes and horizontally acquired prophage/viral ORFs in a single 29-state HMM-Viterbi pass.

1. Sliding 4-kb Local GC Adaptation Across Prophage Islands

Cryptic and lambdoid prophages (CP4-44, CPS-53, e14, Rac, Qin) exhibit sharp local GC drops (34%–44% GC) relative to the 50.8% GC E. coli host background. OrfPredictor computes a prefix-sum 4-kb sliding GC bin (0..43) at every nucleotide so hexamer codon emissions adapt seamlessly across prophage boundaries.

2. Prophage & Host CDS Recall Across All 9 Embedded Islands

Single-pass phage-aware decoding boosts recall across every defective and lambdoid prophage island while simultaneously improving host chromosome 3'-stop recall (98.7% → 99.1%).

3. Operon Overlap Recovery & Single-Pass Decoding Throughput

Phage lysis/lysogeny modules rely on 1-bp (TGATG/TAATG) and 4-bp (ATGA) stop-start overlaps plus short (90–120 bp) accessory ORFs. Direct HMM E → M1 / Er → M1r overlap transitions and intergenic gap rescue capture these without a second decoding pass.
